answer: Vehicle registration makes each extra identity pay one car at the $25,540 used price; a farm running N fakes pays N×$25,540 and cannot share it because a 17-character VIN belongs to one chassis and one owner. A farm stretching one VIN across 500 seats dies by VIN-dedup check at 2: the second filing voids both seats. Repainting changes nothing: a saffron finish keeps the same VIN plate and pigment code, and one duplicate sends a ripple through it, flagging every seat on it. 500 seats need 500 cars: $12.77 million tied up before one fake earns.
